Surah 27, verses 1–6

Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} The Exalted calls His servants' attention to the greatness of the Qur'an, and points to it with a sign that indicates its exaltedness, saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Qur'an, and a Book that makes things clear.﴾ That is: they are the highest of signs, the strongest of proofs, the clearest of indications, and the most manifest in [showing] the most sublime aims, the best objectives, the best deeds, and the purest morals. They are signs that point to true reports, good commands, and the prohibition of every corrupt deed and blameworthy character. They are signs whose clarity and explanation for illuminated insight reach the level of the sun for the eyes. They are signs that establish faith and call toward attaining certainty, and that inform of past and future unseen matters exactly as they were and will be. They are signs that call to knowledge of the Great Lord through His most beautiful names, His highest attributes, and His perfect acts. They are signs that made us acquainted with His messengers and His friends and described them, to the point that it is as if we were looking at them with our own eyes.

{2} Yet, despite this, many of the worlds have not benefited from them, and not all the obstinate have been guided by them, [this is] in order to protect them from one in whom there is no good, no righteousness, and no purity in his heart. Rather, those guided by them are those whom Allah has specially favored with faith, whose hearts are illuminated by it and whose inner selves are purified. Therefore He said: ﴿a guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾. That is: it guides them to follow the straight path, makes clear to them what they should follow or abandon, and gives them the good news of Allah's reward that follows from being guided to this path.

{3} It may be said: perhaps those who claim faith will be many; so is the claim of everyone who says he is a believer accepted, or is there necessarily a proof for it, which is the truth? Therefore the Exalted described the characteristics of the believers, saying: ﴿those who establish the prayer﴾, [meaning] its obligatory and voluntary forms; so they perform its outward acts, its pillars, conditions, and obligations, and also its recommended acts, and its inward acts, which is humility (khushu'), the spirit and essence of prayer, through presence of mind in the nearness of Allah and reflection upon what the one praying says and does. ﴿And they give the zakat﴾: the obligatory zakat to those entitled to it. ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, they are certain﴾. That is: their faith has reached the point of certainty (yaqin), which is complete knowledge that reaches the heart and moves it to action. Their certainty regarding the Hereafter requires the perfection of their striving for it and their caution against the causes of punishment and the things that bring about retribution, and this is the root of all good.

{4} ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾: they deny it and deny the one who brought its affirmation; ﴿We have made their deeds appear attractive to them, so they wander blindly﴾: bewildered, hesitant, preferring Allah's anger over His pleasure, with realities inverted for them, so that they see falsehood as truth and truth as falsehood.

{5} ﴿Those are the ones for whom is the worst torment﴾: that is, its most severe, worst, and greatest form. ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, they are the greatest losers﴾: loss is restricted to them because they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and lost the faith to which the messengers called them.

{6} ﴿And indeed, you are being given the Qur'an from the presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾. That is: this Qur'an that is sent down to you and that you receive comes from One who is All-Wise, who places things in their proper places and situates them in their proper stations, [All-Aware] of the secrets of conditions and their inner realities as well as their outer appearances. And since it comes from One who is All-Wise [and All-Aware], it is known that all of it is wisdom and benefit for the servants, from the One who knows their interests better than they do.

**{7}** That is, mention this noble and honorable state of Musa ibn 'Imran, when the revelation came to him, when he was chosen for his message, and when God spoke to him. When he had stayed in Madyan for several years, he set out with his family from Madyan heading for Egypt. In the course of the journey he lost his way. It was a dark, cold night, and he said to them: ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire﴾, that is, he saw a fire from afar. ﴿I will bring you from it some news﴾ about the road, ﴿or bring you a burning brand that you may warm yourselves﴾, that is, that you may warm yourselves. This is evidence that he was lost and that the cold was severe upon him and his family.

**{8}** ﴿So when he came to it, he was called: "Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it."﴾ That is, God called to him and informed him that this is a sacred, blessed place. Among its blessing is that God made it the place where He spoke to Musa, called to him, and sent him. ﴿And glory be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, exalted above any imputation of deficiency or evil; rather, He is perfect in His attributes and His actions.

**{9}** ﴿O Musa, indeed it is I, God, the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ That is, God informed him that He is God, the one deserving worship alone, with no partner, as in the other verse: ﴿Indeed, I am God; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.﴾ ﴿Al-'Aziz﴾ (the Almighty): the One who subdued all things, to whom all creatures submit. ﴿Al-Hakim﴾ (the Wise): in His command and His creation. Among His wisdom is that He sent His servant Musa ibn 'Imran, whom God knew to be fit for His message, His revelation and His speaking to him. And among His might is that you rely upon Him and do not feel lonely in your solitude or intimidated by the multitude of your enemies and their tyranny, for their forelocks are in the hand of God, and their movements and stillness are under His direction.

**{10}** ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So he threw it down. ﴿Then when he saw it moving as though it were a snake﴾, that is, a jann, which is a term for snakes, swift in motion; ﴿he turned back and did not return﴾, in terror of the snake he saw, in keeping with human nature. So God said to him: ﴿O Musa, do not fear.﴾ And in another verse He said: ﴿Come forward and do not fear; indeed, you are among the secure.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those sent by Me do not fear in My presence﴾, because all fears are contained within His decree, His measure, His disposal and His command. Those whom God has singled out with His message and chosen for His revelation should not fear anyone other than God, especially when they draw nearer to Him and are favored with His speaking to them.

**{11}** ﴿Except one who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil﴾, that is, this is the one who is the object of fear and loneliness, because of the wrong he has committed and the sin that preceded from him. As for the messengers, what have they to do with loneliness and fear? Yet even so, whoever wrongs himself by disobeying God, then repents and turns back, and so God replaces his evil deeds with good deeds and his disobediences with acts of obedience, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful. Let no one despair of His mercy and forgiveness, for He forgives all sins, and He is more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child.

**{12}** ﴿And put your hand into your collar; it will come out white without defect﴾, neither leprosy nor blemish, but a whiteness whose radiance dazzles the beholders, ﴿among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people﴾, that is, these two signs, the turning of the staff into a snake that moves, and the bringing out of the hand from the collar so that it emerges white, are part of nine signs with which you go to Pharaoh and call him and his people. ﴿Indeed, they were a defiant people﴾, who transgressed through their polytheism, their insolence and their haughtiness toward the servants of God, and their arrogance in the land without right.

**{13}** So Musa, peace be upon him, went to Pharaoh and his chiefs, called them to God, and showed them the signs. ﴿So when Our signs came to them as clear sight﴾, that is, luminous, guiding to the truth and by which one sees, as eyes see by the sun, ﴿they said, "This is evident magic."﴾ They were not satisfied merely to say it was magic, but said it was manifest and evident to everyone! This is among the most astonishing of wonders: the signs that give sight and the shining lights are made into the clearest of nonsense and the most evident magic. Is this not the greatest obstinacy and the most brazen sophistry?

**{14}** ﴿And they denied them﴾, that is, they disbelieved in the signs of God, rejecting them. ﴿Though their souls were convinced of them﴾, that is, their denial was not based on doubt or uncertainty, but their denial was with knowledge and certainty of their validity. ﴿Out of wrongdoing﴾ toward the right of their Lord and toward themselves, ﴿and arrogance﴾ against the truth, against the servants, and against submitting to the messengers. ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾: the worst of ends. God destroyed them, drowned them in the sea, disgraced them, and bequeathed their dwellings to the weak among His servants.

This is among the most astonishing of wonders: the signs that give sight and the shining lights are made into the clearest of nonsense and the most evident magic. Is this not the greatest obstinacy and the most brazen sophistry?

**{14}** ﴿And they denied them﴾, that is, they disbelieved in the signs of God, rejecting them. ﴿Though their souls were convinced of them﴾, that is, their denial was not based on doubt or uncertainty, but their denial was with knowledge and certainty of their validity. ﴿Out of wrongdoing﴾ toward the right of their Lord and toward themselves, ﴿and arrogance﴾ against the truth, against the servants, and against submitting to the messengers. ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾: the worst of ends. God destroyed them, drowned them in the sea, disgraced them, and bequeathed their dwellings to the weak among His servants.

**{7}** That is, mention this noble and honorable state of Musa ibn 'Imran, when the revelation came to him, when he was chosen for his message, and when God spoke to him. When he had stayed in Madyan for several years, he set out with his family from Madyan heading for Egypt. In the course of the journey he lost his way. It was a dark, cold night, and he said to them: ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire﴾, that is, he saw a fire from afar. ﴿I will bring you from it some news﴾ about the road, ﴿or bring you a burning brand that you may warm yourselves﴾, that is, that you may warm yourselves. This is evidence that he was lost and that the cold was severe upon him and his family.

**{8}** ﴿So when he came to it, he was called: "Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it."﴾ That is, God called to him and informed him that this is a sacred, blessed place. Among its blessing is that God made it the place where He spoke to Musa, called to him, and sent him. ﴿And glory be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, exalted above any imputation of deficiency or evil; rather, He is perfect in His attributes and His actions.

**{9}** ﴿O Musa, indeed it is I, God, the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ That is, God informed him that He is God, the one deserving worship alone, with no partner, as in the other verse: ﴿Indeed, I am God; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.﴾ ﴿Al-'Aziz﴾ (the Almighty): the One who subdued all things, to whom all creatures submit. ﴿Al-Hakim﴾ (the Wise): in His command and His creation. Among His wisdom is that He sent His servant Musa ibn 'Imran, whom God knew to be fit for His message, His revelation and His speaking to him. And among His might is that you rely upon Him and do not feel lonely in your solitude or intimidated by the multitude of your enemies and their tyranny, for their forelocks are in the hand of God, and their movements and stillness are under His direction.

**{10}** ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So he threw it down. ﴿Then when he saw it moving as though it were a snake﴾, that is, a jann, which is a term for snakes, swift in motion; ﴿he turned back and did not return﴾, in terror of the snake he saw, in keeping with human nature. So God said to him: ﴿O Musa, do not fear.﴾ And in another verse He said: ﴿Come forward and do not fear; indeed, you are among the secure.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those sent by Me do not fear in My presence﴾, because all fears are contained within His decree, His measure, His disposal and His command. Those whom God has singled out with His message and chosen for His revelation should not fear anyone other than God, especially when they draw nearer to Him and are favored with His speaking to them.

**{11}** ﴿Except one who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil﴾, that is, this is the one who is the object of fear and loneliness, because of the wrong he has committed and the sin that preceded from him. As for the messengers, what have they to do with loneliness and fear? Yet even so, whoever wrongs himself by disobeying God, then repents and turns back, and so God replaces his evil deeds with good deeds and his disobediences with acts of obedience, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful. Let no one despair of His mercy and forgiveness, for He forgives all sins, and He is more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child.

**{12}** ﴿And put your hand into your collar; it will come out white without defect﴾, neither leprosy nor blemish, but a whiteness whose radiance dazzles the beholders, ﴿among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people﴾, that is, these two signs, the turning of the staff into a snake that moves, and the bringing out of the hand from the collar so that it emerges white, are part of nine signs with which you go to Pharaoh and call him and his people. ﴿Indeed, they were a defiant people﴾, who transgressed through their polytheism, their insolence and their haughtiness toward the servants of God, and their arrogance in the land without right.

**{13}** So Musa, peace be upon him, went to Pharaoh and his chiefs, called them to God, and showed them the signs. ﴿So when Our signs came to them as clear sight﴾, that is, luminous, guiding to the truth and by which one sees, as eyes see by the sun, ﴿they said, "This is evident magic."﴾ They were not satisfied merely to say it was magic, but said it was manifest and evident to everyone! This is among the most astonishing of wonders: the signs that give sight and the shining lights are made into the clearest of nonsense and the most evident magic. Is this not the greatest obstinacy and the most brazen sophistry?

**{14}** ﴿And they denied them﴾, that is, they disbelieved in the signs of God, rejecting them. ﴿Though their souls were convinced of them﴾, that is, their denial was not based on doubt or uncertainty, but their denial was with knowledge and certainty of their validity. ﴿Out of wrongdoing﴾ toward the right of their Lord and toward themselves, ﴿and arrogance﴾ against the truth, against the servants, and against submitting to the messengers. ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾: the worst of ends. God destroyed them, drowned them in the sea, disgraced them, and bequeathed their dwellings to the weak among His servants.

{15} In this Qur'an, He mentions and highlights His favour upon Dawud (David) and his son Sulayman (Solomon) with wide and abundant knowledge; the indefinite form (in "knowledge") indicates this, as the Exalted said: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field when the sheep of certain people had strayed into it at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment. And We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge...﴾ [21:78–79] to the end of the verse. And they both said, thanking their Lord for His greatest favour in teaching them: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants.﴾ So they praised Allah for making them among the believers, the people of felicity, and that they were among His chosen. There is no doubt that the believers have four ranks: the righteous, above them the martyrs, above them the truthful (siddiqun), and above them the prophets. David and Solomon were among the elite of the messengers, though below the rank of the five possessors of resolve (ulu al-azm), yet they were among the noble, excellent messengers whom Allah mentioned and praised greatly in His Book. So they praised Allah for attaining this station. This is the sign of a servant's felicity: that he be thankful to Allah for His religious and worldly blessings, and that he see all blessings as coming from his Lord; so he does not boast of them nor takes pride in them, but sees that they deserve much gratitude from him.

{16} When He praised them both together, He singled out Sulayman with what was specific to him, because Allah gave him a great kingdom and he had affairs that his father did not have, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both. So He said: ﴿And Sulayman inherited from Dawud﴾; that is, he inherited his knowledge and prophethood, and his father's knowledge was added to his own. Perhaps he learned from his father what was with him of knowledge, along with the knowledge he had at his father's time, as mentioned earlier in His words: ﴿And We gave understanding of it to Solomon﴾. ﴿And he said﴾, thanking Allah and proclaiming His bounty and speaking of His blessing: ﴿O people, we have been taught the speech of birds﴾. He used to understand what they say and speak, just as he conversed with the hoopoe and it conversed with him, and as he understood the speech of the ant to the ants, as will come, and this was not granted to anyone other than Sulayman, peace be upon him. ﴿And we have been given of all things﴾; that is, Allah gave us blessings, means of sovereignty, authority and dominion that He did not give to any of the sons of Adam. For this reason he supplicated his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me﴾. So Allah subjected the devils to him, to work for him in whatever he willed of tasks which others could not accomplish, and subjected the wind to him, its morning course being a month and its evening course a month. ﴿Indeed, this is the clear bounty﴾: that which Allah gave us, favoured us with, and singled us out with; ﴿it is truly the manifest favour﴾: clear and evident. Thus he acknowledged most completely the blessing of Allah, exalted is He.

{17} ﴿And there were gathered for Sulayman his armies of jinn and men and birds, and they were marshalled in ranks﴾: that is, his many, immense and varied hosts of the children of Adam, of the jinn and devils, and of birds were assembled for him. ﴿And they were marshalled in ranks﴾: they were arranged, the first of them being brought back to the last, and they were organised in the utmost order in their marching, halting, descending and travelling. He had prepared for that and made ready his equipment, and all these hosts were obedient to his command, unable to disobey him or rebel against him, as the Exalted said: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾; that is, give without reckoning.

{18} So he travelled with these vast hosts on some of his journeys. ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said﴾, alerting her companions and her kind: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive﴾. So this ant advised and made the ants hear, either by herself, and Allah had given the ants hearing beyond the ordinary, for alerting the ants who filled the valley with the voice of a single ant is one of the most wondrous marvels; or by informing those around her of the ants, and the news spread from some of them to others until it reached all of them, and she commanded them to be cautious and to take the way of that, which is entering their dwellings. She knew the condition of Sulayman and his soldiers and the greatness of his dominion, and she excused them, saying that if they crushed you, it would not be intentionally nor knowingly.

{19} So Sulayman, peace be upon him, heard her words and understood them, ﴿and he smiled, laughing at her speech﴾: in wonder at her eloquence, her advice and her good expression. This is the state of the prophets, peace be upon them: complete courtesy, and wonder in its proper place, and that their laughter should not go beyond a smile; just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's laughter was mostly smiling. For uproarious laughter indicates lightness of mind and bad manners, while not smiling at what is wondrous indicates harshness of character and tyranny, and the messengers are free of that. And he said, thanking Allah who brought him to this state: ﴿My Lord, enable me﴾; that is, inspire me and grant me success ﴿to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents﴾: for blessing upon parents is a blessing upon the child. So he asked his Lord for success in fulfilling the thanks for His religious and worldly blessings upon him and upon his parents. ﴿And that I may do righteousness which You approve﴾; that is, and grant me success to do righteousness which You approve, because it accords with Your command, sincere in it, free from corrupting and deficient matters. ﴿And admit me by Your mercy﴾: among which is Paradise, ﴿among Your righteous servants﴾: for mercy is ordained for the righteous according to their different ranks and stations. This is an example that Allah mentioned of Sulayman's state upon hearing the speech and call of the ant.

{20} Then He mentioned another example of his address to the birds, saying: ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾. This indicates the perfection of his determination and resolve, his good organisation of his hosts, and his personal management of affairs, great and small, to the extent that he did not neglect this matter, which is inspecting the birds and looking to see whether all of them are present or some are missing. This is the meaning of the verse.

Whoever said that he inspected the birds in order to look for the hoopoe, so as to guide him to the nearness and distance of water, as they claimed about the hoopoe that it can see water beneath thick earth, has said nothing of value; for no proof supports this view, rather rational and linguistic evidence indicates its falsehood. As for the rational: it is known from custom, experience and observation that none of these animals has such supernatural sight as to perceive water beneath thick earth; and if it were so, Allah would have mentioned it, for it would be among the greatest signs. As for the linguistic evidence: if this meaning were intended, He would have said, "and he sought the hoopoe to look for water for him, and when he missed him, he said what he said," or "he searched for the hoopoe," or "he looked for him," and similar expressions. Rather, he inspected the birds to see who was present and who was absent, and whether they kept to the stations and places he had assigned them. Furthermore, Sulayman, peace be upon him, did not need or depend on water to the extent that he would need the hoopoe's skill; for he had among the devils and 'afarit those who could dig water for him however deep it might be, and Allah subjected the wind to him, its morning course a month and its evening course a month; so how, with all that, would he need the hoopoe?!

These commentaries which are found and become famous, with which no others are known, transmit these sayings from the Children of Israel unqualified, and the transmitter neglects their contradiction with sound meanings and their application to the sayings. Then they keep circulating, and the later transmitter accepts from the earlier one, until it is thought to be the truth, and so there occurs in the commentaries what bad sayings occur. The intelligent and discerning person knows that this noble Arabic Qur'an, a clear book, with which Allah addressed all creation, its learned and its ignorant, and commanded them to reflect on its meanings and apply them to its Arabic words, whose meanings are well known and which the pure Arabs do not ignore; and when he finds sayings transmitted from other than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he returns them to this principle: if they agree with it, he accepts them, because the wording indicates them; and if they contradict it in wording and meaning, or in wording or meaning, he rejects them and firmly judges them to be false, because he has a known principle that contradicts them, namely what he understands of the meaning and implication of the speech.

The point is that Sulayman's inspecting of the birds and his missing the hoopoe indicates the perfection of his determination and his management of the kingdom personally, and the perfection of his acuteness, to the extent that he missed this small bird: ﴿So he said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?"﴾; that is, is my not seeing him due to my lack of attentiveness to him, because he is hidden among these many nations? Or is he indeed absent, without my permission or command?!

{21} Then he became angry with him and threatened him, saying: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾, short of killing, ﴿or I will slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority﴾; that is, a clear proof of his absence. This was from the perfection of his piety and fairness: he did not swear to a mere punishment of torment or killing, for that would not be except for a sin, and his absence might be due to a clear excuse; therefore he made an exception for it, out of his piety and acuteness.

{22} ﴿So he stayed not long﴾: then he came. This indicates the awe his soldiers had of him and the intensity of their obedience to his command, to the extent that this hoopoe, whom a clear excuse had kept back, could not remain absent for a long time. ﴿And he said﴾ to Sulayman: ﴿I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed﴾; that is, I have knowledge that you have not encompassed, despite your wide knowledge and the height of your rank in it. ﴿And I have come to you from Saba'﴾, the well-known tribe in Yemen, ﴿with certain news﴾; that is, a certain report.

{23} Then he explained this news, saying: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling them﴾; that is, ruling the tribe of Saba', and she is a woman, ﴿and she has been given of all things﴾ that kings are given of wealth, weapons, soldiers, fortresses, castles and the like, ﴿and she has a great throne﴾; that is, the seat of her rule on which she sits is an immense throne, and the greatness of thrones indicates the greatness of the kingdom, the strength of authority and the multitude of men of counsel.

{24} ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah﴾; that is, they are polytheists who worship the sun. ﴿And Satan has made their deeds appear pleasing to them﴾, so they saw what they were upon as the truth, ﴿and so they are not guided﴾: for one who sees that what he is upon is the truth has no hope of his guidance until his belief changes.

{25} Then he said: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, who knows the hidden and concealed in the regions of the heavens and the extents of the earth, from the smallest creatures and the seeds of plants and the secrets of hearts, and who brings forth what is hidden of the earth and heaven by sending down rain and causing plants to grow, and who brings forth what is hidden of the earth at the blowing of the Trumpet and the raising of the dead from the earth, to recompense them for their deeds. ﴿And He knows what you conceal and what you declare.﴾

{26} ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him﴾; that is, worship, devotion, humility and love are fitting only for Him, because He is the one worthy of worship, by reason of His perfect attributes and the blessings that necessitate that. ﴿Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾: which is the ceiling of creation, and encompasses the earth and the heavens. This Sovereign, great in authority and lofty in status, is the One to whom one is humbled, submits, prostrates and bows.

{27–28} So the hoopoe departed when this great news was conveyed to him. Sulayman wondered how it had been hidden from him, and, affirming his perfect intellect and steadiness, said: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or you were among the liars. Go with this letter of mine﴾, whose text will come, ﴿and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them; then observe what they return.﴾ That is, stay back not far away, ﴿and observe what they return﴾ to you and what they send back in reply.

{29–31} So he went with it, delivered it to her, and she said to her people: ﴿Indeed, there has been delivered to me a noble letter﴾; that is, of great worth, from the greatest of the kings of the earth. Then she explained its content, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is from Sulayman, and indeed it reads: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Do not be haughty toward me, but come to me in submission."﴾ That is, do not be above me; rather submit beneath my authority, comply with my commands, and come to me as Muslims. This is in extreme brevity together with complete clarity, for it included his prohibition of exalting himself over him and remaining in their present condition, submission to his command and entry under his obedience, their coming to him, and their invitation to Islam. In it is the recommendation of beginning letters with the full basmalah, and placing the name first in the opening address of the letter.

{32–33} From her wisdom and intellect, she gathered the great men of her state and the men of her kingdom and said: ﴿O eminent ones, advise me in my matter﴾; that is, tell me what we should answer him with. Shall we enter under his obedience and submit, or what shall we do? ﴿I have never decided a matter until you witness﴾; that is, I have never been independent in a matter without your opinion and consultation. ﴿They said, "We are people of strength and people of great might"﴾; that is, if you reject his words and do not enter into his obedience, we are strong in fighting. They seemed inclined to this opinion, which, had it been carried out, would have meant their destruction; but they did not settle on it either, rather they said: ﴿And the decision is yours﴾; that is, the opinion is what you see, knowing her wisdom, her good judgment and her counsel to them. ﴿So see what you will command﴾: with the consideration of reflection and deliberation.

{34–35} She said to them, dissuading them from their opinion and explaining the evil outcome of fighting: ﴿Indeed, when kings enter a town, they ruin it﴾: by killing, taking captives, plundering its wealth and devastating its dwellings, ﴿and they make the honoured of its people humiliated﴾; that is, they make the chiefs, the noble men, into the lowest. That is, this is an unsound opinion. Furthermore, I will not obey him before testing and sending someone to uncover his condition and examine it, and then we will be on insight regarding our affair. She said: ﴿And indeed, I am sending to them a gift, and I will see with what the messengers return﴾ from him: whether he remains on his opinion and his word, or whether the gift deceives him and changes his thinking. And how are his conditions and his soldiers?

{36} So she sent to him a gift with messengers from the wise of her people and the men of opinion among them. ﴿So when Sulayman came﴾; that is, when the messengers came to him with the gift, ﴿he said﴾, disapproving of them and angered at their not responding: ﴿Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you.﴾ It does not weigh with me, nor do I rejoice in it, for Allah has made me independent of it and has multiplied blessings upon me. ﴿Rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾: out of your love for the world and the scarcity of what is in your hands compared to what Allah has given me.

{37} Then he sent back the messenger, without a letter, because he saw in him intelligence and because he would convey his words accurately. He said: ﴿Return to them; we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot withstand, and we will surely expel them from it, humiliated, and they will be debased﴾; that is, they will have no power to resist them. So he returned to them and conveyed what Sulayman had said, and they prepared to march to Sulayman.

{38–40} Sulayman knew that they would certainly march to him, so he said to those present with him of the jinn and men: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾; that is, so that we may dispose of it before they submit, so that their wealth would be respected. ﴿A 'Ifrit of the jinn said﴾: and the 'ifrit is the one who is very strong and energetic: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it.﴾ It appears that Sulayman was at that time in the Levant, and the distance between him and Saba' would be about four months' journey: two months going and two months returning. Yet this 'ifrit says: I undertake to bring it, despite its heaviness and weight and distance, before you rise from the assembly in which you are. The usual length of long gatherings is that they last most of the forenoon, about a third of a day; this is the upper limit of the usual, and it may be less or more. And this is the great king, whose ordinary subjects have such strength and capacity.

Even more eloquent is that "one who had knowledge of the Book" said. The commentators said: he was a righteous, knowledgeable man with Solomon, called Asif ibn Barkhiya, who knew the Greatest Name of Allah, such that when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when asked by it, He gives. ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾ That is, by calling upon Allah with that Name, and it would be present immediately; and he did call upon Allah, and it was present. Allah knows best whether this is the intended meaning, or whether he had knowledge from the Book by which he was able to bring what is far away and accomplish what is difficult.

﴿So when he saw it placed beside him﴾ Solomon ﴿praised Allah for His favors, His sovereignty, and the facilitation of matters for him, and said, "This is of the bounty of my Lord to test me: whether I will be grateful or ungrateful."﴾ That is, to test me with it. Peace be upon him was not deceived by his kingdom, authority, and power as is the custom of ignorant kings; rather, he knew that this was a test from his Lord, and he feared that he would not fulfill the duty of thanking for this blessing. Then he explained that this gratitude does not benefit Allah; its benefit returns to its doer. So he said: ﴿And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾ Free of need of his deeds, Generous, abundant in goodness, which encompasses both the grateful and the ungrateful; however, thankfulness for His blessings is a means of increasing them, and ingratitude for them is a means of their loss.

{41} Then he said to those with him: ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾; that is, alter it by adding and removing. ﴿We will see﴾: testing her intellect: ﴿Will she be guided﴾ to the correct answer and have the intelligence and discernment befitting her kingship, ﴿or will she be among those who are not guided?﴾

{42} ﴿So when she came﴾ arriving before Solomon, he presented her throne to her, and her last sight of it had been when she left it in her land. ﴿It was said to her, "Is your throne like this?"﴾ That is, it has become known to us that you have a great throne; is it like this throne which we have brought for you? ﴿She said, "It is as if it were it."﴾ This was from her intelligence and discernment: she did not say "it is it," because of the change and alteration in it, and she did not deny that it was it, because she recognized it; so she gave an expression that admits both possibilities and is true in both states.

Solomon then said, amazed at her guidance and intellect, and thankful to Allah for having given him something greater than her: ﴿And we were given knowledge before her﴾; that is, guidance, intellect, and firm judgment before this queen. ﴿And we were Muslims﴾: which is the beneficial, original guidance.

It is possible that this is from the speech of the Queen of Sheba: "And we were given knowledge of the kingdom of Solomon, his authority, and the increase of his power before this state in which we saw his ability to bring the throne from a great distance; so we submitted to him and came as Muslims, submitting to his authority."

{43} Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that which she worshipped besides Allah prevented her﴾; that is, from Islam. Otherwise, she had the intelligence and discernment by which she could distinguish truth from falsehood, but false beliefs take away the insight of the heart. ﴿Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.﴾ So she continued upon their religion, and for an individual to separate from the people of the religion and the established custom, and to hold a view by his own reason regarding their error and mistake, is among the rarest things; therefore, her remaining in disbelief is not strange.

{44} Then Solomon wished that she would see from his authority what would dazzle the minds, so he commanded her to enter the ṣarḥ, which is the elevated, spacious assembly hall, and it was an assembly hall of glass, with rivers flowing beneath it. ﴿It was said to her, "Enter the ṣarḥ." And when she saw it, she thought it was a pool﴾ of water, because glass is transparent, so the water beneath it appears as if it were flowing by itself with nothing between. ﴿And she uncovered her shins﴾ for wading; and this too was from her intellect and manners. For she did not refuse to enter the place she had been commanded to enter, knowing that she had only been summoned for honor, and that Solomon's kingdom and its organization were founded upon wisdom, and there was not in her heart the slightest doubt of any evil situation after what she had seen. When she prepared to wade, it was said to her: ﴿Indeed, it is a ṣarḥ paved smooth﴾; that is, an assembly hall ﴿of glass﴾; so there is no need for you to uncover your shins. Then, when she reached Solomon and witnessed what she witnessed, and knew his prophethood and messengership, she repented and turned back from her disbelief and ﴿said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

This is what Allah has related to us of the story of the Queen of Sheba and what happened to her with Solomon. As for what lies beyond that, the derived branches and the Israelite narratives, they are not connected to the interpretation of the words of Allah, and they are among the matters whose certainty can only be established by known, infallible evidence; and the reports on this subject, all or most of them, are not of that kind. So the utmost caution is to disregard them and not include them in the tafsirs. And Allah knows best.

{15} In this Qur'an, He mentions and highlights His favour upon Dawud (David) and his son Sulayman (Solomon) with wide and abundant knowledge; the indefinite form (in "knowledge") indicates this, as the Exalted said: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field when the sheep of certain people had strayed into it at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment. And We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge...﴾ [21:78–79] to the end of the verse. And they both said, thanking their Lord for His greatest favour in teaching them: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants.﴾ So they praised Allah for making them among the believers, the people of felicity, and that they were among His chosen. There is no doubt that the believers have four ranks: the righteous, above them the martyrs, above them the truthful (siddiqun), and above them the prophets. David and Solomon were among the elite of the messengers, though below the rank of the five possessors of resolve (ulu al-azm), yet they were among the noble, excellent messengers whom Allah mentioned and praised greatly in His Book. So they praised Allah for attaining this station. This is the sign of a servant's felicity: that he be thankful to Allah for His religious and worldly blessings, and that he see all blessings as coming from his Lord; so he does not boast of them nor takes pride in them, but sees that they deserve much gratitude from him.

{16} When He praised them both together, He singled out Sulayman with what was specific to him, because Allah gave him a great kingdom and he had affairs that his father did not have, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both. So He said: ﴿And Sulayman inherited from Dawud﴾; that is, he inherited his knowledge and prophethood, and his father's knowledge was added to his own. Perhaps he learned from his father what was with him of knowledge, along with the knowledge he had at his father's time, as mentioned earlier in His words: ﴿And We gave understanding of it to Solomon﴾. ﴿And he said﴾, thanking Allah and proclaiming His bounty and speaking of His blessing: ﴿O people, we have been taught the speech of birds﴾. He used to understand what they say and speak, just as he conversed with the hoopoe and it conversed with him, and as he understood the speech of the ant to the ants, as will come, and this was not granted to anyone other than Sulayman, peace be upon him. ﴿And we have been given of all things﴾; that is, Allah gave us blessings, means of sovereignty, authority and dominion that He did not give to any of the sons of Adam. For this reason he supplicated his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me﴾. So Allah subjected the devils to him, to work for him in whatever he willed of tasks which others could not accomplish, and subjected the wind to him, its morning course being a month and its evening course a month. ﴿Indeed, this is the clear bounty﴾: that which Allah gave us, favoured us with, and singled us out with; ﴿it is truly the manifest favour﴾: clear and evident. Thus he acknowledged most completely the blessing of Allah, exalted is He.

{17} ﴿And there were gathered for Sulayman his armies of jinn and men and birds, and they were marshalled in ranks﴾: that is, his many, immense and varied hosts of the children of Adam, of the jinn and devils, and of birds were assembled for him. ﴿And they were marshalled in ranks﴾: they were arranged, the first of them being brought back to the last, and they were organised in the utmost order in their marching, halting, descending and travelling. He had prepared for that and made ready his equipment, and all these hosts were obedient to his command, unable to disobey him or rebel against him, as the Exalted said: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾; that is, give without reckoning.

{18} So he travelled with these vast hosts on some of his journeys. ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said﴾, alerting her companions and her kind: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive﴾. So this ant advised and made the ants hear, either by herself, and Allah had given the ants hearing beyond the ordinary, for alerting the ants who filled the valley with the voice of a single ant is one of the most wondrous marvels; or by informing those around her of the ants, and the news spread from some of them to others until it reached all of them, and she commanded them to be cautious and to take the way of that, which is entering their dwellings. She knew the condition of Sulayman and his soldiers and the greatness of his dominion, and she excused them, saying that if they crushed you, it would not be intentionally nor knowingly.

{19} So Sulayman, peace be upon him, heard her words and understood them, ﴿and he smiled, laughing at her speech﴾: in wonder at her eloquence, her advice and her good expression. This is the state of the prophets, peace be upon them: complete courtesy, and wonder in its proper place, and that their laughter should not go beyond a smile; just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's laughter was mostly smiling. For uproarious laughter indicates lightness of mind and bad manners, while not smiling at what is wondrous indicates harshness of character and tyranny, and the messengers are free of that. And he said, thanking Allah who brought him to this state: ﴿My Lord, enable me﴾; that is, inspire me and grant me success ﴿to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents﴾: for blessing upon parents is a blessing upon the child. So he asked his Lord for success in fulfilling the thanks for His religious and worldly blessings upon him and upon his parents. ﴿And that I may do righteousness which You approve﴾; that is, and grant me success to do righteousness which You approve, because it accords with Your command, sincere in it, free from corrupting and deficient matters. ﴿And admit me by Your mercy﴾: among which is Paradise, ﴿among Your righteous servants﴾: for mercy is ordained for the righteous according to their different ranks and stations. This is an example that Allah mentioned of Sulayman's state upon hearing the speech and call of the ant.

{20} Then He mentioned another example of his address to the birds, saying: ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾. This indicates the perfection of his determination and resolve, his good organisation of his hosts, and his personal management of affairs, great and small, to the extent that he did not neglect this matter, which is inspecting the birds and looking to see whether all of them are present or some are missing. This is the meaning of the verse.

Whoever said that he inspected the birds in order to look for the hoopoe, so as to guide him to the nearness and distance of water, as they claimed about the hoopoe that it can see water beneath thick earth, has said nothing of value; for no proof supports this view, rather rational and linguistic evidence indicates its falsehood. As for the rational: it is known from custom, experience and observation that none of these animals has such supernatural sight as to perceive water beneath thick earth; and if it were so, Allah would have mentioned it, for it would be among the greatest signs. As for the linguistic evidence: if this meaning were intended, He would have said, "and he sought the hoopoe to look for water for him, and when he missed him, he said what he said," or "he searched for the hoopoe," or "he looked for him," and similar expressions. Rather, he inspected the birds to see who was present and who was absent, and whether they kept to the stations and places he had assigned them. Furthermore, Sulayman, peace be upon him, did not need or depend on water to the extent that he would need the hoopoe's skill; for he had among the devils and 'afarit those who could dig water for him however deep it might be, and Allah subjected the wind to him, its morning course a month and its evening course a month; so how, with all that, would he need the hoopoe?!

These commentaries which are found and become famous, with which no others are known, transmit these sayings from the Children of Israel unqualified, and the transmitter neglects their contradiction with sound meanings and their application to the sayings. Then they keep circulating, and the later transmitter accepts from the earlier one, until it is thought to be the truth, and so there occurs in the commentaries what bad sayings occur. The intelligent and discerning person knows that this noble Arabic Qur'an, a clear book, with which Allah addressed all creation, its learned and its ignorant, and commanded them to reflect on its meanings and apply them to its Arabic words, whose meanings are well known and which the pure Arabs do not ignore; and when he finds sayings transmitted from other than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he returns them to this principle: if they agree with it, he accepts them, because the wording indicates them; and if they contradict it in wording and meaning, or in wording or meaning, he rejects them and firmly judges them to be false, because he has a known principle that contradicts them, namely what he understands of the meaning and implication of the speech.

The point is that Sulayman's inspecting of the birds and his missing the hoopoe indicates the perfection of his determination and his management of the kingdom personally, and the perfection of his acuteness, to the extent that he missed this small bird: ﴿So he said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?"﴾; that is, is my not seeing him due to my lack of attentiveness to him, because he is hidden among these many nations? Or is he indeed absent, without my permission or command?!

{21} Then he became angry with him and threatened him, saying: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾, short of killing, ﴿or I will slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority﴾; that is, a clear proof of his absence. This was from the perfection of his piety and fairness: he did not swear to a mere punishment of torment or killing, for that would not be except for a sin, and his absence might be due to a clear excuse; therefore he made an exception for it, out of his piety and acuteness.

{22} ﴿So he stayed not long﴾: then he came. This indicates the awe his soldiers had of him and the intensity of their obedience to his command, to the extent that this hoopoe, whom a clear excuse had kept back, could not remain absent for a long time. ﴿And he said﴾ to Sulayman: ﴿I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed﴾; that is, I have knowledge that you have not encompassed, despite your wide knowledge and the height of your rank in it. ﴿And I have come to you from Saba'﴾, the well-known tribe in Yemen, ﴿with certain news﴾; that is, a certain report.

{23} Then he explained this news, saying: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling them﴾; that is, ruling the tribe of Saba', and she is a woman, ﴿and she has been given of all things﴾ that kings are given of wealth, weapons, soldiers, fortresses, castles and the like, ﴿and she has a great throne﴾; that is, the seat of her rule on which she sits is an immense throne, and the greatness of thrones indicates the greatness of the kingdom, the strength of authority and the multitude of men of counsel.

{24} ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah﴾; that is, they are polytheists who worship the sun. ﴿And Satan has made their deeds appear pleasing to them﴾, so they saw what they were upon as the truth, ﴿and so they are not guided﴾: for one who sees that what he is upon is the truth has no hope of his guidance until his belief changes.

{25} Then he said: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, who knows the hidden and concealed in the regions of the heavens and the extents of the earth, from the smallest creatures and the seeds of plants and the secrets of hearts, and who brings forth what is hidden of the earth and heaven by sending down rain and causing plants to grow, and who brings forth what is hidden of the earth at the blowing of the Trumpet and the raising of the dead from the earth, to recompense them for their deeds. ﴿And He knows what you conceal and what you declare.﴾

{26} ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him﴾; that is, worship, devotion, humility and love are fitting only for Him, because He is the one worthy of worship, by reason of His perfect attributes and the blessings that necessitate that. ﴿Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾: which is the ceiling of creation, and encompasses the earth and the heavens. This Sovereign, great in authority and lofty in status, is the One to whom one is humbled, submits, prostrates and bows.

{27–28} So the hoopoe departed when this great news was conveyed to him. Sulayman wondered how it had been hidden from him, and, affirming his perfect intellect and steadiness, said: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or you were among the liars. Go with this letter of mine﴾, whose text will come, ﴿and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them; then observe what they return.﴾ That is, stay back not far away, ﴿and observe what they return﴾ to you and what they send back in reply.

{29–31} So he went with it, delivered it to her, and she said to her people: ﴿Indeed, there has been delivered to me a noble letter﴾; that is, of great worth, from the greatest of the kings of the earth. Then she explained its content, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is from Sulayman, and indeed it reads: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Do not be haughty toward me, but come to me in submission."﴾ That is, do not be above me; rather submit beneath my authority, comply with my commands, and come to me as Muslims. This is in extreme brevity together with complete clarity, for it included his prohibition of exalting himself over him and remaining in their present condition, submission to his command and entry under his obedience, their coming to him, and their invitation to Islam. In it is the recommendation of beginning letters with the full basmalah, and placing the name first in the opening address of the letter.

{32–33} From her wisdom and intellect, she gathered the great men of her state and the men of her kingdom and said: ﴿O eminent ones, advise me in my matter﴾; that is, tell me what we should answer him with. Shall we enter under his obedience and submit, or what shall we do? ﴿I have never decided a matter until you witness﴾; that is, I have never been independent in a matter without your opinion and consultation. ﴿They said, "We are people of strength and people of great might"﴾; that is, if you reject his words and do not enter into his obedience, we are strong in fighting. They seemed inclined to this opinion, which, had it been carried out, would have meant their destruction; but they did not settle on it either, rather they said: ﴿And the decision is yours﴾; that is, the opinion is what you see, knowing her wisdom, her good judgment and her counsel to them. ﴿So see what you will command﴾: with the consideration of reflection and deliberation.

{34–35} She said to them, dissuading them from their opinion and explaining the evil outcome of fighting: ﴿Indeed, when kings enter a town, they ruin it﴾: by killing, taking captives, plundering its wealth and devastating its dwellings, ﴿and they make the honoured of its people humiliated﴾; that is, they make the chiefs, the noble men, into the lowest. That is, this is an unsound opinion. Furthermore, I will not obey him before testing and sending someone to uncover his condition and examine it, and then we will be on insight regarding our affair. She said: ﴿And indeed, I am sending to them a gift, and I will see with what the messengers return﴾ from him: whether he remains on his opinion and his word, or whether the gift deceives him and changes his thinking. And how are his conditions and his soldiers?

{36} So she sent to him a gift with messengers from the wise of her people and the men of opinion among them. ﴿So when Sulayman came﴾; that is, when the messengers came to him with the gift, ﴿he said﴾, disapproving of them and angered at their not responding: ﴿Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you.﴾ It does not weigh with me, nor do I rejoice in it, for Allah has made me independent of it and has multiplied blessings upon me. ﴿Rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾: out of your love for the world and the scarcity of what is in your hands compared to what Allah has given me.

{37} Then he sent back the messenger, without a letter, because he saw in him intelligence and because he would convey his words accurately. He said: ﴿Return to them; we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot withstand, and we will surely expel them from it, humiliated, and they will be debased﴾; that is, they will have no power to resist them. So he returned to them and conveyed what Sulayman had said, and they prepared to march to Sulayman.

{38–40} Sulayman knew that they would certainly march to him, so he said to those present with him of the jinn and men: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾; that is, so that we may dispose of it before they submit, so that their wealth would be respected. ﴿A 'Ifrit of the jinn said﴾: and the 'ifrit is the one who is very strong and energetic: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it.﴾ It appears that Sulayman was at that time in the Levant, and the distance between him and Saba' would be about four months' journey: two months going and two months returning. Yet this 'ifrit says: I undertake to bring it, despite its heaviness and weight and distance, before you rise from the assembly in which you are. The usual length of long gatherings is that they last most of the forenoon, about a third of a day; this is the upper limit of the usual, and it may be less or more. And this is the great king, whose ordinary subjects have such strength and capacity.

Even more eloquent is that "one who had knowledge of the Book" said. The commentators said: he was a righteous, knowledgeable man with Solomon, called Asif ibn Barkhiya, who knew the Greatest Name of Allah, such that when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when asked by it, He gives. ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾ That is, by calling upon Allah with that Name, and it would be present immediately; and he did call upon Allah, and it was present. Allah knows best whether this is the intended meaning, or whether he had knowledge from the Book by which he was able to bring what is far away and accomplish what is difficult.

﴿So when he saw it placed beside him﴾ Solomon ﴿praised Allah for His favors, His sovereignty, and the facilitation of matters for him, and said, "This is of the bounty of my Lord to test me: whether I will be grateful or ungrateful."﴾ That is, to test me with it. Peace be upon him was not deceived by his kingdom, authority, and power as is the custom of ignorant kings; rather, he knew that this was a test from his Lord, and he feared that he would not fulfill the duty of thanking for this blessing. Then he explained that this gratitude does not benefit Allah; its benefit returns to its doer. So he said: ﴿And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾ Free of need of his deeds, Generous, abundant in goodness, which encompasses both the grateful and the ungrateful; however, thankfulness for His blessings is a means of increasing them, and ingratitude for them is a means of their loss.

{41} Then he said to those with him: ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾; that is, alter it by adding and removing. ﴿We will see﴾: testing her intellect: ﴿Will she be guided﴾ to the correct answer and have the intelligence and discernment befitting her kingship, ﴿or will she be among those who are not guided?﴾

{42} ﴿So when she came﴾ arriving before Solomon, he presented her throne to her, and her last sight of it had been when she left it in her land. ﴿It was said to her, "Is your throne like this?"﴾ That is, it has become known to us that you have a great throne; is it like this throne which we have brought for you? ﴿She said, "It is as if it were it."﴾ This was from her intelligence and discernment: she did not say "it is it," because of the change and alteration in it, and she did not deny that it was it, because she recognized it; so she gave an expression that admits both possibilities and is true in both states.

Solomon then said, amazed at her guidance and intellect, and thankful to Allah for having given him something greater than her: ﴿And we were given knowledge before her﴾; that is, guidance, intellect, and firm judgment before this queen. ﴿And we were Muslims﴾: which is the beneficial, original guidance.

It is possible that this is from the speech of the Queen of Sheba: "And we were given knowledge of the kingdom of Solomon, his authority, and the increase of his power before this state in which we saw his ability to bring the throne from a great distance; so we submitted to him and came as Muslims, submitting to his authority."

{43} Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that which she worshipped besides Allah prevented her﴾; that is, from Islam. Otherwise, she had the intelligence and discernment by which she could distinguish truth from falsehood, but false beliefs take away the insight of the heart. ﴿Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.﴾ So she continued upon their religion, and for an individual to separate from the people of the religion and the established custom, and to hold a view by his own reason regarding their error and mistake, is among the rarest things; therefore, her remaining in disbelief is not strange.

{44} Then Solomon wished that she would see from his authority what would dazzle the minds, so he commanded her to enter the ṣarḥ, which is the elevated, spacious assembly hall, and it was an assembly hall of glass, with rivers flowing beneath it. ﴿It was said to her, "Enter the ṣarḥ." And when she saw it, she thought it was a pool﴾ of water, because glass is transparent, so the water beneath it appears as if it were flowing by itself with nothing between. ﴿And she uncovered her shins﴾ for wading; and this too was from her intellect and manners. For she did not refuse to enter the place she had been commanded to enter, knowing that she had only been summoned for honor, and that Solomon's kingdom and its organization were founded upon wisdom, and there was not in her heart the slightest doubt of any evil situation after what she had seen. When she prepared to wade, it was said to her: ﴿Indeed, it is a ṣarḥ paved smooth﴾; that is, an assembly hall ﴿of glass﴾; so there is no need for you to uncover your shins. Then, when she reached Solomon and witnessed what she witnessed, and knew his prophethood and messengership, she repented and turned back from her disbelief and ﴿said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

This is what Allah has related to us of the story of the Queen of Sheba and what happened to her with Solomon. As for what lies beyond that, the derived branches and the Israelite narratives, they are not connected to the interpretation of the words of Allah, and they are among the matters whose certainty can only be established by known, infallible evidence; and the reports on this subject, all or most of them, are not of that kind. So the utmost caution is to disregard them and not include them in the tafsirs. And Allah knows best.

{15} In this Qur'an, He mentions and highlights His favour upon Dawud (David) and his son Sulayman (Solomon) with wide and abundant knowledge; the indefinite form (in "knowledge") indicates this, as the Exalted said: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field when the sheep of certain people had strayed into it at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.
