So Allah is better than what they associate with Him.

Then He mentioned the details by which it is known, and it is determined, that He is the God who is worthy of worship, and that worshipping Him is the truth while worshipping anything other than Him is falsehood. So He said:

{60} That is: Is the One who created the heavens and what is in them, such as the sun, the moon, the stars and the angels, and the earth and what is in it, such as mountains, seas, rivers, trees and other things, {and sent down for you} — that is, for your sake — {water from the sky, and We made to grow therewith} — that is, gardens {full of delight} — that is, of pleasing appearance, due to the abundance and variety of their trees and the goodness of their fruits. {You could never have made grow their trees} — were it not for Allah's favour upon you in sending down rain. {Is there a god along with Allah?} — who did these deeds, that He should be worshipped alongside Him and associated with Him? {Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals} — to Him others, and make others equal to Him, while they know that He alone is the Creator of the upper and lower worlds and the Sender of provision.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verse 61:

{61} That is: Are idols and images, deficient in every respect, which create nothing, provide no sustenance and bring no benefit, better, or is it God who {made the earth a place of settlement}: a place where servants can settle, and be established upon it to dwell, cultivate, build, and go and come; {and made rivers through it}; that is, He placed within the earth rivers from which servants benefit for their crops, their trees, their drinking, and the watering of their livestock; {and made for it firm mountains}; that is, mountains that anchor it and hold it fast, lest it sway, and serve as pegs for it, lest it be disturbed; {and made a barrier between the two seas}: the salt sea and the sweet sea; {a barrier}: which prevents their mixing, so that the benefit intended from each of them would otherwise be lost. Rather, He placed between them a barrier of land; He caused the courses of the rivers in the earth to be distant from the seas, so that their intended purposes and benefits are achieved. {Is there a god with God?}: Did He do that so that God be equated with Him and associated with Him in worship? {Nay, but most of them do not know}: so they associate others with God by blindly following their leaders. Otherwise, had they known with true knowledge, they would not have associated anything with Him.

{62} That is: Who answers the distressed one, whom calamities have troubled and whose need has become difficult, and who is compelled to seek deliverance from what he is in, except Allah alone? And who removes the evil (i.e., the affliction, the harm, and the calamity), except Allah alone? And who makes you successors (khulafa') on the earth, granting you authority over it, providing you with sustenance, and bringing His bounties to you, and you are successors of those before you, just as He will cause you to die and bring forth another people after you? Is there a god along with Allah who does these deeds? No one does any of that along with Allah, even by your own admission, O polytheists. For this reason, when harm touched them, they called upon Allah, making their religion sincerely His, because they knew that He alone is capable of repelling and removing it. "Little do you remember" means: little is your remembrance and reflection upon matters which, if you remembered them, you would take heed and return to guidance. But heedlessness and turning away have encompassed you, and therefore you neither desisted nor were guided.

{63} That is: Who guides you when you are in the darknesses of land and sea, where there is no guide and no landmark visible, and no means of deliverance except His guidance to you, His facilitating the way for you, and His making for you the means by which you are guided?! {And who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy}; that is: before the rain. He sends them, and they stir up the clouds, then they gather them together, then they bring them together, then they impregnate them, then they pour them out, so the servants rejoice at this before the rain falls. {Is there a god with Allah?} who did that?! Or is it He alone who has singled Himself out for it?! Why, then, do you associate others with Him and worship other than Him?! {Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him}: He is magnified, glorified and sanctified above their polytheism and their equating of other than Him with Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verse 64:

{64} That is: Who is it that originates creation, brings created things into being, begins their creation, and then restores creation on the Day of Resurrection and the Gathering?! {And who provides for you from the heaven and the earth} with rain and vegetation?! {Is there a god along with Allah?} Who does that and has power over it? {Say: "Bring your proof, if you are truthful."} That is: bring your argument and your evidence for what you have claimed. {If you are truthful.} And otherwise, supposing you say that the idols have some partnership with Him in any of that, then that is mere assertion; confirm it with proof. And otherwise, know that you are falsifiers with no argument, so return to the certain evidences and the decisive proofs which indicate that Allah is the One alone in all acts of disposal, and that He is the one deserving that all kinds of worship be directed to Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verse 65–69:

{65} He, may He be exalted, informs that He alone has knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth, as in His saying: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a clear record.﴾ And as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs...﴾ to the end of the surah. These unseen matters and the like are exclusive to Allah in knowledge. No angel brought near, nor any prophet sent, knows them. And since He alone has knowledge of these things, and His knowledge encompasses the inner secrets, the hidden thoughts and the concealed things, He is the One for whom alone worship is fitting.

Then He, may He be exalted, informs about the weakness of the knowledge of those who deny the Hereafter, moving from one matter to what is more emphatic than it. He said: ﴿And they do not perceive﴾; that is, they do not know ﴿when they will be resurrected﴾; that is, when the resurrection, the rising up and the standing up from the graves will be. That is, for this reason they have not prepared themselves.

{66} ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter﴾; that is, rather, it has become weak and diminished, and it was not certainty nor knowledge that reached the heart. This is the lowest and least degree of knowledge: its weakness and feebleness. Rather, they have no knowledge at all, not even weak knowledge. Rather, ﴿they are in doubt about it﴾; that is, about the Hereafter. Doubt removes knowledge, since knowledge in all its degrees does not coexist with doubt. ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾; that is, concerning the Hereafter: their insight has become blinded to it, and there is in their hearts no acceptance of its occurrence and no possibility of it, but rather they deny it and deem it far-fetched.

{67} For this reason He said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "When we have become dust and our fathers as well, will we really be brought forth?"﴾; that is, this is far-fetched and not possible. They measured the power of the One of complete power by their weak powers.

{68} ﴿Indeed, we have been promised this, we and our fathers before. This is nothing but the tales of the former peoples﴾; that is, the resurrection. ﴿We and our fathers before﴾; that is, it has not come to us, and we have not seen anything of it. ﴿This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples﴾; that is, their stories and reports by which time is passed, which have no basis and no truth in them.

He moved, in describing the state of those who deny, from informing that they do not know when the time of the Hereafter is, to informing of the weakness of their knowledge of it, then informing that it is doubt, then informing that it is blindness, then informing of their denial of it and their deeming its occurrence far-fetched. That is, because of these states, the fear of the Hereafter has departed from their hearts; so they proceeded into the disobedience of Allah, it became easy for them to deny the truth and affirm falsehood, and they made lawful the desires while neglecting the acts of worship, and so they lost their worldly life and their Hereafter.

{69} Then He alerted them to the truthfulness of what the messengers had reported, saying: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the criminals."﴾ So you will not find a criminal who persisted in his crime except that his end was the worst of ends, and Allah brought upon him the evil and punishment fitting his condition.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verses 73–75:

{73} He alerts His servants to the vastness of His generosity and the abundance of His bounties, and urges them to thank Him for them. Yet despite this, most people have turned away from gratitude and have become preoccupied with the blessings rather than the Bestower of them.

{74} {And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal} — that is, what is hidden within {their breasts} — {and what they reveal}. So let them beware of the One who knows the hidden and the apparent, and let them be mindful of Him.

{75} {And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven or earth} — that is, a hidden matter and a secret among the secrets of the higher and lower worlds — {except that it is in a clear register}. That Register encompasses everything that has happened and will happen until the Hour is established. Thus every event that occurs, whether manifest or hidden, is in full accordance with what has been written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verses 76–77:**

{76} This is a report about the Qur'an's dominance (*haymanah*) over the earlier scriptures, and its detailing and clarifying of what was in them that had become confused and disputed among the Children of Israel. This Qur'an recounts it in a way that removes the ambiguity, and it explains the correct position on the disputed matters.

{77} Since it has this degree of greatness and clarity, and removes every disagreement and resolves every difficulty, it is the greatest of God's blessings upon His servants. However, not everyone meets this blessing with gratitude. For this reason, He made clear that its benefit, its light, and its guidance are specific to the believers, so He said: {And indeed it is guidance}, from misguidance, error, and doubts, {and a mercy}, by which their hearts find peace and their religious and worldly affairs are set right, {for the believers}, those who affirm it, who receive it with acceptance, who turn to reflect upon it, and who ponder its meanings. For these, guidance to the straight path is attained through it, along with the mercy that entails happiness, success, and prosperity.

{78} That is: Indeed, Allah the Exalted will decide between those who dispute and will judge between those who differ with His just judgment and His equitable decree. He will recompense each one according to what He knows of it.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verses 79–81:

{79} That is: rely upon your Lord in bringing about benefits and warding off harms, in conveying the message, establishing the religion, and striving against the enemies. {Indeed, you are upon the manifest truth}: clear. The one who is upon the truth, calls to it, and stands in defense of it is more worthy than others of reliance upon God, for he strives in a matter that is certain, whose truthfulness is known, with no doubt or dispute about it. Moreover, it is truth in its utmost clarity, with no obscurity or ambiguity in it.

{80} When you have done what you were charged with and have relied upon God in that, the straying of those who stray will not harm you, nor is it your responsibility to guide them. Therefore He said: {Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call} — that is, when you call them and summon them — {especially when they turn away, retreating}: for that is more emphatic in their not hearing.

{81} {Nor can you guide the blind away from their error}: as the Exalted said: {Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills} [Qur'an 28:56]. {You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are submissive}: that is, those who submit to you, who believe in God's verses and yield to them through their deeds and their surrender, as the Exalted said: {Only those who listen will respond. As for the dead, God will raise them, then to Him they will be returned} [Qur'an 6:36].

So the manifestation of this creature by Allah is one of His wondrous signs, in order to make clear to the people that which they had been disputing (yamtarun). This is the well-known creature that will emerge at the end of time and will be among the portents of the Hour (ashrat al-sa'ah), as the hadiths have multiplied concerning it. [Allah and His Messenger did not mention the manner of this creature; they mentioned only its effect and its purpose, and that it is one of the signs of Allah. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verses 83–85:

{83} He, exalted is He, informs about the state of those who denied on the Day of Resurrection, and that Allah gathers them and assembles from every nation a company and a group, {of those who deny Our signs, and they will be driven in order}: the first of them is gathered up to the last of them, and the last up to the first, so that questioning, rebuke and blame may encompass them all.

{84} {Until, when they have arrived}: and been present, He will say to them, rebuking and reproaching them: {Did you deny My signs while you had not encompassed them in knowledge?}; that is, it was obligatory upon you to pause until the truth became clear to you, and not to speak except with knowledge. So how could you deny a matter you had not encompassed in knowledge? {Or what was it that you used to do?}; that is, He asks them about their knowledge and their deeds, and He finds their knowledge to be a denial of the truth and their deeds to be for other than Allah, or upon other than the sunnah of their messenger.

{85} {And the word will be fulfilled against them because of what they wronged}; that is, the word of punishment has become binding upon them because of their wrongdoing, which they persisted in, and the proof has been established against them. {So they will not be able to speak}: because they have no argument.

{86} That is: have they not seen this great sign and immense blessing, namely that God has subjected to them the night and the day? This one, with its darkness, so that they may rest in it, relieve themselves of fatigue, and prepare for work; and that one, with its light, so that they may disperse through it for their livelihood and their dealings. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾: [signs] of the perfection of God's oneness and the abundance of His blessing.

{87} Exalted is He, warning His servants of what lies before them of the Day of Resurrection, with its trials, its distresses, and the things that unsettle hearts. He says: ﴿And the Day when the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾, by reason of the blowing into it. That is: they will be alarmed and dismayed, and some of them will surge against others, out of fear of what precedes it. ﴿Except whom Allah wills﴾: those whom Allah has honored, made steadfast, and protected from the terror. ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾: all of creation, at the blowing of the Horn, will come abased and submissive. As He, exalted, says: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾. On that Day, leaders and followers will be equal in humiliation and submission to the Owner of the Kingdom.

{88} And from its awfulness: ﴿You see the mountains, thinking them fixed﴾: you lose nothing of them, and you suppose them to remain in their customary state, while in fact hardships and terrors have reached them to the utmost extent. They will be broken into pieces, then they will vanish and become ﴿dust dispersed﴾. Therefore He says: ﴿And they pass by as the clouds pass﴾: because of their lightness and the intensity of that fear. That is ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who perfected everything; indeed He is Acquainted with what you do﴾: He will recompense you for your deeds.

{89} Then He explains the manner of its recompense, saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾: a generic noun, encompassing every good deed, whether of speech, action, or heart. ﴿For him is better than it﴾ [﴿fa-lahu ʿashru amthālihā﴾, "for him is ten times the like of it"]: this is the minimum of multiplication. ﴿And they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe﴾; that is, from the matter by which creation is terrified they will be secure, even though they may be terrified along with them.

{90} ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾: a generic noun encompassing every evil deed, ﴿their faces will be thrown into the Fire﴾; that is, they will be cast into the Fire upon their faces, and it will be said to them: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾

{87} Exalted is He, warning His servants of what lies before them of the Day of Resurrection, with its trials, its distresses, and the things that unsettle hearts. He says: ﴿And the Day when the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾, by reason of the blowing into it. That is: they will be alarmed and dismayed, and some of them will surge against others, out of fear of what precedes it. ﴿Except whom Allah wills﴾: those whom Allah has honored, made steadfast, and protected from the terror. ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾: all of creation, at the blowing of the Horn, will come abased and submissive. On that Day, leaders and followers will be equal in humiliation and submission to the Owner of the Kingdom.

They will be broken into pieces, then they will vanish and become ﴿dust dispersed﴾. Therefore He says: ﴿And they pass by as the clouds pass﴾: because of their lightness and the intensity of that fear. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 27, verses 91–93:

{91} That is: Say to them, O Muhammad, "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city," meaning Makkah the Honored, "who has made it sacred and has bestowed favors upon its people; so it is incumbent upon them to respond to that with gratitude and acceptance." {And to Him belongs everything}: of the higher and lower things. He mentioned this so that it would not be imagined that His lordship is restricted to the House alone. "And I have been commanded that I should be among the Muslims"; that is, that I should hasten to Islam. And he (ﷺ) did so, for he was the first of this Ummah to embrace Islam and the greatest of them in submission.

{92} {And} I have also been commanded {to recite the Qur'an} to you, so that you may be guided by it, follow it, and learn its words and meanings. This is what is incumbent upon me, and I have conveyed it. {Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own self}: its benefit returns to him and its fruit comes back to him. {And whoever goes astray, say, "I am only one of the warners"}: and the guidance is not in my hand at all.

{93} {And say, "All praise is for Allah"}: to whom belongs all praise in this world and the Hereafter, and from all creation, especially the people of distinction and the elite among His servants. For the praise and commendation of their Lord that has occurred from them, and that which should occur from them, is greater than that which occurs from others, because of the elevation of their ranks, the completeness of their nearness to Him, and the abundance of His bounties upon them. {He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them}: a recognition by which you will be guided to truth and falsehood. He will surely show you of His signs that you may be illumined by them in darknesses, so that whoever perishes does so upon clear evidence and whoever lives does so upon clear evidence. {And your Lord is not unaware of what you do}: rather, He knows what you are upon of deeds and states, and He knows the measure of the recompense for those deeds, and He will judge between you with a judgment you will praise Him for, and you will have no argument against Him in any way whatsoever.

The commentary on Surat an-Naml is completed by the grace, help and facilitation of Allah. We ask the Exalted that His kindness and assistance never cease to be continuous upon us and reach us from Him, for He is the Most Generous of the generous, the best of the merciful, the one who connects those who are cut off, the answerer of those who ask, the facilitator of difficult matters, the opener of the doors of His blessings, the one who bestows His gifts abundantly at all times, the one who makes the Qur'an easy for those who remember, and who makes its paths and doors easy for those who turn to it, and who extends the table of His goodness and generosity to those who reflect. And all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, his family and companions, and grant them peace.

By the hand of its compiler and dictator, Abdul-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Abdullah as-Sa'di, may Allah forgive him, his parents, and all Muslims. This was on the 22nd of Ramadan, 1343 AH. Its transcription from the handwriting of its author was completed on the 29th of Dhu al-Hijjah, 1346 AH.
